is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluates insecticide efficacy against Anopheles arabiensis and Anopheles gambiae s.s. (page 3, 5).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for the Vgsc L995S (kdr-east) mutation (page 5, 12).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 12 states: 'In the first hut trial 87 mosquitoes were analysed... 85 mosquitoes were homozygous susceptible (SSe) and 2 mosquitoes did not amplify. For the second hut trial 100 mosquitoes were analysed... 99/100 were homozygous kdr susceptible'.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses wild, free-flying mosquitoes collected in the Harusini field station, Moshi, Tanzania (page 3, 5).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an experimental hut trial conducted by the authors (page 1, 3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Harusini field station, Moshi rural district, Kilimanjaro region, Tanzania (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The trials were conducted between September 2017 and February 2019 (page 9).

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a specific experimental hut trial evaluating a new insecticide formulation (broflanilide) and is not part of a larger surveillance network dataset.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts, are provided in the main text (page 12).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of broflanilide (TENEBENAL) in experimental huts in Moshi, Tanzania. It included cone assays with insectary-reared strains and collections of wild Anopheles arabiensis. Genotyping for the kdr-east (L1014S) mutation was performed on a subset of the wild-caught mosquitoes.
